stem.text: Determine whether the power series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{\left(x - 2\right)^{n}}{5^{n} n^{\frac{1}{3}}} \) converges or diverges at the right endpoint of its interval of convergence, naming the test used.

answer_key.label: At \( x = 7 \) the series diverges by the p-series test, because \( p = \frac{1}{3} \le 1 \).

worked_solution.text: The ratio test gives convergence for \( \left|x - 2\right| < 5 \), so the right endpoint is \( x = 7 \).
At \( x = 7 \), \( \frac{\left(x - 2\right)^{n}}{5^{n}} = \left(\frac{5}{5}\right)^{n} = 1 \), so the series becomes \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{\frac{1}{3}}} \).
It is a p-series with \( p = \frac{1}{3} \le 1 \).
At \( x = 7 \) the series diverges by the p-series test, because \( p = \frac{1}{3} \le 1 \), so \( x = 7 \) does not belong to the interval of convergence.

options.label: At \( x = 7 \) the series diverges by the ratio test, because \( -3 < x < 7 \) leaves it out.
options.derivation: the endpoint never examined: the open interval from the ratio test taken as the whole answer

options.label: At \( x = 7 \) the series diverges by the p-series test, because \( p = \frac{1}{3} \le 1 \).
At \( x = 7 \) the series converges by the alternating series test, because the sizes \( \frac{1}{n^{\frac{1}{3}}} \) decrease to 0.
options.derivation: the alternating series test used on the endpoint series although its terms are all positive

options.label: At \( x = 7 \) the series converges by the p-series test, because \( p = \frac{1}{3} < 1 \).
options.derivation: the p-series threshold misapplied, p less than 1 read as convergence
